description: "How to drive the running Obsidian app programmatically over CDP to verify plugin changes, and where the fuller Playwright harness lives"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01fc3963-d706-437b-b51d-c4c4cfa1c803
  modified: 2026-09-08T01:24:16.291Z
---

Obsidian is Electron, so it can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Relaunch with
`open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222`, then attach over
`ws` to the target from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list`. Verified working August 2026 on
Obsidian 1.8.4 / macOS — 23/23 assertions driving the ENG-2113 search footer.

Key points learned the hard way:

- **Attach to an already-open vault** instead of rewriting `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`
  to select one. The rewrite is how PR #959 selects a vault and it is also that PR's worst bug —
  if launch throws afterwards, teardown never runs and the user's global Obsidian config stays clobbered.
- Several CDP page targets exist (devtools, popouts, one per vault). Pick by
  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- **Force the renderer active over CDP instead of fighting for window focus.** Two calls at connect
  time make occlusion throttling irrelevant:
  `Page.setWebLifecycleState {state:"active"}` and `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled {enabled:true}`.
  Without them, `osascript -e 'tell application "Obsidian" to activate'` only holds until the next
  command returns focus to the terminal, and Reading view silently renders an **empty**
  `.markdown-preview-section` — links, Properties and backlinks all absent, no error. Verified
  September 2026 on Obsidian 1.13.7: the identical scenario went from `body link rendered: false`
  to `true` with those two calls added. The note below still describes the underlying throttling.
- **The Obsidian window must be visible (`document.visibilityState === "visible"`) while scenarios
  run.** When it is covered/minimised/on another Space, Chromium throttles the renderer's timers —
  100 ms → 300–900 ms, and after ~5 min hidden to once per minute — so anything built on
  `setTimeout` (a 500 ms save debounce, a sync debounce, a poll loop *inside* the page) silently
  stalls. It presents as "the feature is broken" (writes land minutes later) with zero errors.
  ENG-2107 lost an hour to this. Check `visibilityState` and a 100 ms timer's real latency before
  believing a timing failure; `electronWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` helps only until focus changes,
  so ask the user to click the window and poll `visibilityState` before firing the scenario.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.
- **`editor.hasFocus()` is not measurable from CDP.** It reads `false` even for a plain
  `editor.focus()` with no modal involved and `document.hasFocus() === true`; no element holds DOM
  focus at all (`document.activeElement` is the top-level app div). Take a **baseline** measurement
  of the same assertion outside the feature under test before believing a focus failure — ENG-2114
  looked like a focus regression until the baseline failed identically. Assert the observable
  consequence instead (cursor position advanced past the inserted text).
- **Stale `.modal-container` elements poison selectors.** A scenario that times out or throws leaves
  its modal in the DOM, so the next run's `querySelector(".modal-container .modal")` reads the *old*
  modal — producing "footer missing the action" and "modal did not close" failures while the feature
  actually works. Start every scenario with
  `document.querySelectorAll(".modal-container").forEach(el => el.remove())`.
- The plugin **folder** is `discourse-graphs` but the **id** is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; passing the
  folder name to `disablePlugin`/`enablePlugin` silently no-ops (`loaded: false`, `manifests[folder]`
  undefined). Read the real id from `app.plugins.manifests`, whose `dir` field maps id → folder.

- `detachLeavesOfType("markdown")` followed by `getLeaf(true)` throws **"No tab group found."** —
  detaching the last markdown leaf destroys the tab group the new leaf would go in. Reuse
  `getMostRecentLeaf()` instead of clearing first.
- Obsidian's **Properties** block and the **backlinks-in-document** panel contain **no
  `a.internal-link` anchors**: a link property renders as `div.multi-select-pill-content.internal-link`
  and backlink entries carry no anchors at all. A markdown post processor that queries
  `a.internal-link` therefore cannot leak into either, whatever it scans. Both panels are also
  collapsed/`display:none` by default, so a scenario must expand Properties
  (`.metadata-properties-heading`) and run `backlink:toggle-backlinks-in-document` before asserting.
- **A markdown post processor receives its element DETACHED (`el.isConnected === false`) during a
  normal Reading view render**, but attached and inside `.modal-container` when the plugin calls
  `MarkdownRenderer.render` itself. So `el.closest(".markdown-reading-view")` is null on the real
  path and is the wrong guard; `el.closest(".modal-container")` is the correct tell for "this is our
  own modal preview". Measured with a throwaway `registerMarkdownPostProcessor` probe pushing to a
  `window.__probe` array — a cheap pattern for any question about post processor call context.
- zsh expands `${VAR}` inside `node -e "..."`, silently turning `plugins['${ID}']` into `plugins['']`.
  Write the scenario to a `.mjs` file instead of passing it through `-e`.

A fuller Playwright + CDP harness already exists on branch
`worktree-eng-1583-automate-obsidian-dev-environment-load-and-visual-validation` (PR #959, ENG-1583):
launch, vault switching, command palette driving, modal helpers, step screenshots. It is open with
CHANGES_REQUESTED — the blocking objection is documentation quality, not the mechanism — and is far
behind main. Reuse its `e2e/helpers/obsidian-setup.ts` rather than rediscovering the launch tricks.

Unrelated dev-loop gotcha hit while doing this: editing only a file under `apps/obsidian/src/styles/`
never triggers a rebuild, because the concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd` while those files sit
outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file to force it. See [[feedback-obsidian-no-console]] for the
related Notice-instead-of-console rule in this app.

  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- **Force the renderer active over CDP instead of fighting for window focus.** Two calls at connect
  time make occlusion throttling irrelevant:
  `Page.setWebLifecycleState {state:"active"}` and `Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled {enabled:true}`.
  Without them, `osascript -e 'tell application "Obsidian" to activate'` only holds until the next
  command returns focus to the terminal, and Reading view silently renders an **empty**
  `.markdown-preview-section` — links, Properties and backlinks all absent, no error. Verified
  September 2026 on Obsidian 1.13.7: the identical scenario went from `body link rendered: false`
  to `true` with those two calls added. The note below still describes the underlying throttling.
- **The Obsidian window must be visible (`document.visibilityState === "visible"`) while scenarios
  run.** When it is covered/minimised/on another Space, Chromium throttles the renderer's timers —
  100 ms → 300–900 ms, and after ~5 min hidden to once per minute — so anything built on
  `setTimeout` (a 500 ms save debounce, a sync debounce, a poll loop *inside* the page) silently
  stalls. It presents as "the feature is broken" (writes land minutes later) with zero errors.
  ENG-2107 lost an hour to this. Check `visibilityState` and a 100 ms timer's real latency before
  believing a timing failure; `electronWindow.setAlwaysOnTop(true)` helps only until focus changes,
  so ask the user to click the window and poll `visibilityState` before firing the scenario.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.
- **`editor.hasFocus()` is not measurable from CDP.** It reads `false` even for a plain
  `editor.focus()` with no modal involved and `document.hasFocus() === true`; no element holds DOM
  focus at all (`document.activeElement` is the top-level app div). Take a **baseline** measurement
  of the same assertion outside the feature under test before believing a focus failure — ENG-2114
  looked like a focus regression until the baseline failed identically. Assert the observable
  consequence instead (cursor position advanced past the inserted text).
- **Stale `.modal-container` elements poison selectors.** A scenario that times out or throws leaves
  its modal in the DOM, so the next run's `querySelector(".modal-container .modal")` reads the *old*
  modal — producing "footer missing the action" and "modal did not close" failures while the feature
  actually works. Start every scenario with
  `document.querySelectorAll(".modal-container").forEach(el => el.remove())`.
- The plugin **folder** is `discourse-graphs` but the **id** is `@discourse-graph/obsidian`; passing the
  folder name to `disablePlugin`/`enablePlugin` silently no-ops (`loaded: false`, `manifests[folder]`
  undefined). Read the real id from `app.plugins.manifests`, whose `dir` field maps id → folder.

- `detachLeavesOfType("markdown")` followed by `getLeaf(true)` throws **"No tab group found."** —
  detaching the last markdown leaf destroys the tab group the new leaf would go in. Reuse
  `getMostRecentLeaf()` instead of clearing first.
- Obsidian's **Properties** block and the **backlinks-in-document** panel contain **no
  `a.internal-link` anchors**: a link property renders as `div.multi-select-pill-content.internal-link`
  and backlink entries carry no anchors at all. A markdown post processor that queries
  `a.internal-link` therefore cannot leak into either, whatever it scans. Both panels are also
  collapsed/`display:none` by default, so a scenario must expand Properties
  (`.metadata-properties-heading`) and run `backlink:toggle-backlinks-in-document` before asserting.
- **A markdown post processor receives its element DETACHED (`el.isConnected === false`) during a
  normal Reading view render**, but attached and inside `.modal-container` when the plugin calls
  `MarkdownRenderer.render` itself. So `el.closest(".markdown-reading-view")` is null on the real
  path and is the wrong guard; `el.closest(".modal-container")` is the correct tell for "this is our
  own modal preview". Measured with a throwaway `registerMarkdownPostProcessor` probe pushing to a
  `window.__probe` array — a cheap pattern for any question about post processor call context.
- zsh expands `${VAR}` inside `node -e "..."`, silently turning `plugins['${ID}']` into `plugins['']`.
  Write the scenario to a `.mjs` file instead of passing it through `-e`.

A fuller Playwright + CDP harness already exists on branch
`worktree-eng-1583-automate-obsidian-dev-environment-load-and-visual-validation` (PR #959, ENG-1583):
launch, vault switching, command palette driving, modal helpers, step screenshots. It is open with
CHANGES_REQUESTED — the blocking objection is documentation quality, not the mechanism — and is far
behind main. Reuse its `e2e/helpers/obsidian-setup.ts` rather than rediscovering the launch tricks.

Unrelated dev-loop gotcha hit while doing this: editing only a file under `apps/obsidian/src/styles/`
never triggers a rebuild, because the concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd` while those files sit
outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file to force it. See [[feedback-obsidian-no-console]] for the
related Notice-instead-of-console rule in this app.

content.text:
I couldn't reproduce your bug on this branch in testVault. Datacore finishes indexing in about a quarter of a second, which is too fast to explain a modal that fails every time you first open it. It's probably something else, or a much bigger vault.

## How long does Datacore take to index?

| Case in testVault (~445 files) | Search API available | Index ready | Window where queries come back empty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Startup (restarting the Datacore plugin, index already cached) | ~60 ms | ~253 ms | ~190 ms |
| Full reindex | immediately | ~256 ms | ~200 ms |

During that window, Datacore's search API is already usable but its index isn't finished, so a raw query returned **0** Question nodes instead of 17. That's what `main` shows in the modal, and what this PR's fallback fixes. The time grows with vault size, so a vault with thousands of notes could take seconds.

## What I tested (all on this branch, Datacore ready)

Every one of these returned results on the very first query:
- Open from the command palette, then type immediately with real keystrokes (47 results)
- Pick Question first, click back into the title field, then type (6 results)
- Type first, then pick Question
- Pick Claim, then Question, then type
- Right-click selected text → **Turn into discourse node → Question**. The type was preselected and the text prefilled, with 7 results

I ruled out the focus handling: the title field really has focus when the modal opens, and the dropdown opens without an extra click. Datacore's index and Obsidian's metadata cache also returned the same node counts for every type.

## What would narrow it down

1. **Which build did you see it on?** I installed this branch into testVault today at 14:48. If you saw the bug on an older or `main` build, the Datacore race is a plausible cause. If you can still reproduce it now, the race isn't the cause, because this branch falls back to the metadata cache.
2. **Does retyping fix it, or only switching the node type?** If retyping fixes it, the first query came back empty, which points to indexing timing. If only switching the node type fixes it, something is wrong with the initial node type state in the modal.
3. **Which entry point, and which vault?** I didn't test the canvas openers or the inline node type picker.
4. **How soon after launching Obsidian?**

Side effects in testVault: I restarted the Datacore plugin, forced one reindex (which only rebuilds its cache), and reloaded the DG plugin. I selected a word in `Synthesis.md` but didn't change its contents, and closed every modal without submitting. The CDP scripts are in the scratchpad if you want me to rerun any case against your exact steps.

content.text:
Whether it fixes your bug depends on what causes it, which we don't know yet. It can't make the bug worse, and it only changes what the search returns, not when the modal searches.

The create-node modal searches through `searchDiscourseNodesByTitle`, one of the three lookups this PR changes. So:

| If your bug is caused by… | Effect of merging |
|---|---|
| **Datacore still indexing** when you first search (just after launch, or in a large vault) | **Fixes it.** The first search falls back to the metadata cache instead of returning nothing. "Switching type makes it work" fits this: the second search runs after indexing finishes. |
| **Datacore ready but its results briefly out of date**, e.g. a note created seconds ago | **No effect.** The PR deliberately trusts an empty result once Datacore is ready. |
| **Something in the modal itself**, like the initial node type state or when the search effect fires | **No effect.** The PR doesn't touch `ModifyNodeModal.tsx`. |
| **Datacore not installed** | Not your bug, since on `main` search would then *always* be empty, not just the first time. The PR does fix that case. |

I couldn't reproduce it with Datacore ready, and in testVault the indexing window is only about 0.2 s. So the first row is plausible but unproven for your case, and I wouldn't call it the fix.

A quick way to tell is to reproduce it on the build that's in testVault now, which is this branch:
- **If the bug is gone**, it was the indexing race, and this PR fixes it.
- **If it still happens**, it's a separate bug in the modal, and the PR only adds safety elsewhere.

Checking whether retyping (not just switching the node type) also fixes it would narrow it further.

content.text:
I fixed all six lint warnings this PR added in `apps/obsidian/src/services/QueryEngine.ts`. The change is uncommitted; I haven't committed or pushed it yet.

**What changed** (1 file, 19 lines added, 19 removed, formatted with Prettier):
- **4 unnecessary casts:** `getFileCache(...)?.frontmatter as Record<string, unknown> | undefined` is now a type annotation, the same way `getDiscourseNodeCandidates` already does it.
- **`String(rawExistingRelations)`:** the fallback now keeps only string relation entries instead of stringifying whatever is there.
